facts.claim: no one has grown one [an arbuscular fungus] to completion on a laboratory plate without a plant present
facts.problem: Slightly outdated rather than wrong. Since 2019-2020 (Kameoka et al.; Sugiura et al., PNAS) Rhizophagus irregularis has been grown axenically through to infective secondary spores when supplied with a fatty acid (myristate), which actually confirms the passage's mechanism. The absolute 'no one has' could be softened to 'without a plant or a supplied fatty acid'. Low stakes; no question depends on it.
